topics.title: Adaptive retrieval and corrective RAG
topics.research_question: How do adaptive retrieval, retrieval-quality assessment, and evidence verification improve RAG faithfulness, and what are their costs and failure boundaries?

critical_papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity

questions: Which signals trigger retrieval, correction, or stopping?
Does each corrective action address retrieval relevance, generation faithfulness, or both?
Which datasets, models, metrics, and ablations support the reported improvements?
What latency and tool-call cost accompanies the quality improvement over standard RAG?
Which failure cases show that evidence quality cannot be judged reliably?
exclusions: Product marketing without a citable technical artifact.
Private-only settings that omit datasets, metrics, and evaluation protocol.

topics.title: GraphRAG for global and multi-hop questions
topics.research_question: Do graph-enhanced RAG methods provide reproducible gains over vector RAG for global synthesis and multi-hop questions?

critical_papers.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation

questions: How are graph nodes, edges, and indexes constructed?
How does each work define local, global, or multi-hop questions?
Do graph and vector baselines share models, corpora, prompts, and budgets?
Are index cost, query latency, and failure rate reported alongside quality?
Which claims rely only on abstracts or model judges?
exclusions: Concept papers without a vector baseline.
Materials that conflate citation graphs with generated semantic graphs.
Demos that omit model, corpus, or evaluation settings.

topics.title: Reliability of RAG evaluation
topics.research_question: How do RAG evaluation frameworks measure retrieval quality, faithfulness, and answer relevance, and when can their results be misleading?

critical_papers.title: RAGAs: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

questions: Does each metric require gold answers, gold contexts, or an LLM judge?
Can retrieval and generation metrics localize the failing layer?
What bias arises when judge and generator use the same model family?
How is agreement with human judgment established?
How should quality, latency, tokens, and cost be combined in a fair comparison?
exclusions: Studies reporting only one aggregate automatic score.
LLM-judge studies that omit prompts or scoring scales.
Experiments that tune and report final results on the same development set.

topics.title: RAG security and corpus poisoning
topics.research_question: How can malicious documents, indirect prompt injection, or retrieval manipulation control RAG outputs, and which defenses have reproducible evidence?

critical_papers.title: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
Benchmarking and Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
RAG security survey or benchmark seed

questions: Which layer does the attacker control: corpus, query, ranker, or generation context?
How is attack success defined, and what happens to normal-query quality?
Does the defense rely on document trust, retrieval anomaly detection, or generation constraints?
Does the defense survive adaptive attacks and model transfer?
How can logs retain audit evidence without reproducing malicious content?
exclusions: Single jailbreak conversations without an attack model and success criterion.
Materials that require executing embedded malicious instructions.
Private test sets that cannot be audited or legally accessed.

claim_evidence_examples.evidence: Specifically, a lightweight retrieval evaluator is designed to assess the overall quality of retrieved documents for a query, returning a confidence degree based on which different knowledge retrieval actions can be triggered.
claim_evidence_examples.claim: CRAG uses a lightweight retrieval evaluator to assess retrieved-document quality and trigger different retrieval actions from its confidence signal.
claim_evidence_examples.limitation: This evidence does not establish perfect evaluator accuracy or a universal hallucination reduction.
